verdict.stance: Neutral / Fortress-Balance-Sheet LNG Giant Amid Hormuz & Ras Laffan Shock (AA Neg)
verdict.summary: H126 revenue dropped 35% YoY to QAR 87bn and net profit fell 69% to QAR 15bn following the March 2026 Ras Laffan strike and Strait of Hormuz disruptions, prompting Fitch to place QatarEnergy's AA rating on Negative outlook (mirroring Qatar sovereign). Balance sheet remains fortress-grade (QAR 704bn assets vs QAR 184bn total liabilities, SCP aa+) with no bond maturities until 2031.

positives: Fortress balance sheet: QAR 704bn assets vs QAR 184bn total liabilities (SCP aa+ at Fitch) and $1.5bn Sep-26 bond cleanly retired.
World's lowest-cost North Field LNG reserve base with $11bn bond curve locked in at 2.25%–3.30% through 2031–2051.
H126 operating cash flow resilient at QAR 21bn despite severe operational shock.
negatives: Acute Middle East geopolitical/conflict exposure: Mar-26 Ras Laffan LNG infrastructure damage and Strait of Hormuz export disruptions.
Fitch AA Negative outlook reflecting prolonged export-route vulnerability.
Heavy multi-year North Field expansion capex requirements.
